name: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX)
description: Sarbanes-Oxley Act — U.S. federal law establishing requirements for financial reporting and internal controls for publicly traded companies. Section 404 is the primary IT compliance driver.

controls.title: Section 302 — Corporate Responsibility for Financial Reports
controls.description: CEO and CFO must personally certify the accuracy of financial reports and the effectiveness of internal controls. Disclosures must include any significant changes in internal controls.

controls.title: Section 404 — Management Assessment of Internal Controls
controls.description: Management must include in annual reports an assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls over financial reporting. External auditors must attest to management's assessment.

controls.title: Section 409 — Real Time Disclosure
controls.description: Companies must disclose material changes in financial condition or operations on a rapid and current basis.

controls.title: IT General Controls — Change Management
controls.description: Changes to IT systems must be authorized, tested, and approved before promotion to production. Emergency changes must follow defined procedures and be reviewed after implementation.

controls.title: IT General Controls — Logical Access
controls.description: Access to financial applications and data must be restricted to authorized personnel. User access must be reviewed periodically. Segregation of duties must be enforced.

controls.title: IT General Controls — Computer Operations
controls.description: IT operations must ensure availability and reliability of systems supporting financial reporting. Incident management, backup, and recovery procedures must be established.

controls.title: IT General Controls — Data Center Physical Security
controls.description: Physical access to data centers and computer rooms housing financial systems must be restricted to authorized personnel.

controls.title: IT General Controls — Program Development
controls.description: Development and implementation of new applications and major system changes must follow a defined system development lifecycle.

controls.title: IT Application Controls — Input Controls
controls.description: Data entered into financial applications must be complete, accurate, and authorized. Input validation controls must exist to prevent erroneous data entry.

controls.title: IT Application Controls — Processing Controls
controls.description: Processing of financial data must be complete, accurate, and authorized. Processing controls must detect and reject erroneous transactions.

controls.title: IT Application Controls — Output Controls
controls.description: Output from financial applications must be complete, accurate, distributed only to authorized recipients, and reconciled to input.

controls.title: Audit Trail and Log Retention
controls.description: Complete and accurate audit trails must be maintained for financial transactions and access to financial systems for at least 7 years.

controls.title: Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity
controls.description: Business continuity and disaster recovery plans for financial systems must be documented, tested, and maintained.
